skill.name: creating-feedback-loops

skill.summary: Create structured review cycles that turn feedback and recurring issues into measurable improvements.

content.value_statement: Repeated mistakes weaken AI-assisted work and make improvement difficult to measure. This skill creates review cycles, checkpoints, issue logs, and metrics for systematic refinement.
actual_capabilities: Selects immediate, interactive, checkpoint, or pattern-learning loops for a task.
Defines baseline metrics for correctness, completeness, quality, efficiency, and user satisfaction.
Creates self-review checklists, quality gates, and checkpoint workflows.
Structures issue logs, pattern analyses, prevention strategies, and learning logs.
Compares baseline and current measures to verify improvements and define stopping criteria.
limitations: Provides process guidance and templates but does not execute tests or validate outcomes.
Does not retain learning across sessions unless the user stores logs externally.
Uses illustrative metrics that require replacement with verified project data.
Cannot determine correctness or user satisfaction without evidence and feedback.

use_cases.title: Improve Code Review Cycles
use_cases.description: Create checkpoints and quality gates for multi-file implementation work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Retrospectives
use_cases.description: Turn recurring defects and feedback into tracked patterns, prevention actions, and measurable follow-up.

use_cases.title: Refine Recurring Content
use_cases.description: Use iterative reviews and audience feedback to improve clarity, completeness, and consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Self-Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an immediate feedback loop for [task]. Include a short checklist, a correction step, and clear completion criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a focused task that needs one review before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Add Project Checkpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Design checkpoints for [project] at key milestones. For each checkpoint, define evidence, quality questions, corrective actions, and continuation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a project with several dependent stages.

prompt_templates.title: Track Recurring Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a pattern-learning loop for [workflow]. Include an issue log, a root-cause method, prevention actions, owners, and review frequency.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when similar defects appear across repeated work.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Measured Improvement System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full feedback system for [process]. Define baselines, metrics, collection points, quality gates, iteration rules, and verification methods.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an established process that needs measurable, ongoing improvement.

output_examples.input: Create a feedback loop for API endpoint implementation.
output: Checkpoint: verify requirements, input validation, errors, tests, and security after each endpoint.
Record defects by category and compare counts after three endpoints.
Continue only when required tests pass and no critical issue remains.

output_examples.input: Help a support team reduce incomplete customer replies.
output: Baseline: review 20 replies for missing questions, unclear actions, and absent ownership.
Quality gate: every reply addresses each question and names the next action.
Review the same measures weekly and update the checklist when patterns change.

output_examples.input: Set up a learning log for recurring research summaries.
output: Log missed evidence, unclear conclusions, excessive detail, and reader corrections.
Group repeated issues monthly and identify one prevention action for each pattern.
Compare reviewer edits against the baseline before adopting a new process.

best_practices: Start with a small set of metrics tied to user-visible quality.
Collect evidence at consistent points and compare results with a documented baseline.
Review the feedback loop and remove steps that add overhead without useful insight.
anti_patterns: Do not treat illustrative metric values as measured results.
Do not continue iterating after agreed quality criteria are met.
Do not record user data or sensitive content in issue logs without authorization.

faq.question: What feedback loop types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers immediate self-review, user-driven iteration, milestone checkpoints, and learning from recurring patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill remember lessons across sessions?
faq.answer: No. Cross-session learning requires an external log or another authorized storage method.

faq.question: Can it measure improvement automatically?
faq.answer: No. It defines metrics and comparison methods, but users must provide reliable observations and results.

faq.question: How should I choose metrics?
faq.answer: Choose a few measures linked to the task, available evidence, and user-visible outcomes.

faq.question: Does it execute tests or quality tools?
faq.answer: No. It recommends verification steps but does not run commands or external tools.

faq.question: When should an iteration cycle stop?
faq.answer: Stop when agreed quality gates pass, requirements are complete, and further changes offer little measurable benefit.
